subtype: Teen growth spurt appetite and grumpiness [Actor]
passage: Zeenat, you know how I bit your head off yesterday about the project? I've figured something out. I've shot up this year; every pair of trousers is short, and I'm hungry all the time. When dinner's late at home, I turn into a different person. Last Sunday Papa asked about my marks before we'd eaten, and I shouted that he never lets me breathe. Then I had a big plate of rajma chawal and felt human again, and embarrassed. It's the same pattern every time: empty stomach, short fuse, blaming whoever's closest. So I've started saying, "Give me a bit, I have to eat first, then we can talk." Papa actually laughed and said, "Fine, Lokesh, food first." And I keep peanuts in my bag now. So, sorry about yesterday. I was starving, and you got the worst of me.

qa.q: What does Lokesh now keep in the bag?
How did Lokesh feel after eating on Sunday?
qa.a: Lokesh felt human again but also embarrassed about shouting at Papa.

qa.q: What is useful about Lokesh's new line about eating before talking?
qa.a: It names the hunger early, so Lokesh can refuel before a hard conversation instead of blaming whoever is closest.

qa.q: How might Zeenat feel hearing this?
qa.a: Zeenat may feel relieved to get an apology and an explanation, and less hurt about being snapped at over the project.

grounding: Shows a growing teenager who turns sharp when meals are late recognising the pattern and asking to eat before talking.

subtype: Teen growth spurt appetite and grumpiness [Actor]
passage: I'm Sarika, Ankita's older sister, and this year I've watched her grow out of every pair of jeans she owns. At our cousin's wedding in Jaipur, lunch kept getting pushed back for the rituals. By afternoon Ankita had rolled her eyes at Bua, told me my dupatta looked "tragic" and was sitting alone on the steps, chin on her knees. I couldn't tell if she was sad about something bigger. Then she stood up and said, quite calmly, "Sarika di, I'm not angry with anyone. I just need food before I talk to people." We found the snacks counter, and she ate a plate of samosas. Soon she was dancing with the little cousins, and she went back to say sorry to Bua.

qa.q: What did Ankita say about Sarika's dupatta?
What does Ankita's calm line suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She felt low and cranky from hunger, but was aware that it was not really anger at anyone.

qa.q: Which choice turned the afternoon around, and why?
qa.a: Ankita saying she needed food before talking and then eating; it met her body's need instead of letting the grumpiness land on relatives.

qa.q: How does Sarika see Ankita's moodiness at first?
qa.a: Sarika cannot tell whether it is sadness about something bigger, and only understands once Ankita names the hunger.

grounding: Illustrates a growing teenager getting sharp and low when a meal is delayed, then recognising it and asking to eat before talking.
